title: Backup/Restore Cost Model — Storage Growth + Egress Estimates (Redwood Private)
content:
Sheet: Backup storage + egress estimates for Redwood Private Day-2 toolkit
Owner: Bruno
Last updated: 2025-02-18

Purpose
- Provide an order-of-magnitude cost model for backup artifact storage growth + restore/DR egress implications.
- Used by Infra/SRE + Solutions to set customer expectations and recommend default retention.
- This is NOT a billing quote. Customer cloud pricing, discount tiers, and regional pricing will vary.

Scope of what this sheet assumes is in “control-plane backup” artifact
- Control-plane config DB snapshot (Postgres physical backup or equivalent)
- etcd snapshot (where applicable / when we own it; for managed control planes this may be “N/A”)
- Kubernetes resource export (namespaced manifests + Helm values) — small but included
- Backup manifest + checksums + metadata

Explicit exclusions (modeled as 0 unless customer opts in)
- Model weights / data-plane caches (expected stateless)
- Customer application data
- Long-term audit log retention (separate exporter + retention guidance)

Key assumptions (edit these numbers per customer)
A) Backup schedule (default assumptions)
- Backup frequency: 1 backup/day (nightly)
- Restore drill cadence: 1 restore/week in staging (pulls 1 artifact)

B) Size multipliers
- Compression factor (avg): 0.60 (i.e., 40% reduction)
  - Note: Postgres physical backups compress reasonably; high-entropy payloads compress poorly.
- Encryption + packaging overhead: 1.03 (tar metadata + manifest + padding)
- Safety buffer for transient storage during creation: +1x artifact size on backup node (ephemeral / local disk)

C) Pricing (placeholders; update per customer region)
- S3 Standard storage: $0.023 / GB-month
- S3 Standard egress to internet/other region: $0.09 / GB
- Cross-region replication data transfer (simplified): treat as egress-like $0.02–$0.09 / GB depending on provider
- NFS/on-prem storage: priced as $/TB-month varies widely; not included here (customer-owned infra)
- KMS costs: ignored (usually negligible vs storage/egress at these volumes; call out if extreme key ops)

Deployment archetypes + component sizes (inputs)
(These are reference “Private control plane” sizes we’ve observed/assumed; tune per account.)

Table 1 — Reference component sizes and churn
| Deployment size | Tenants / scale (rough) | Config DB logical size (GB) | Daily change rate | etcd snapshot (GB) | k8s export (GB) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Small (S) | <= 50 tenants, low QPS | 20 | 2% | 5 | 0.2 |
| Medium (M) | 50–200 tenants | 80 | 2% | 20 | 0.3 |
| Large (L) | 200–1000 tenants | 300 | 1.5% | 50 | 0.5 |

Notes:
- Daily change rate is included for incremental/WAL sensitivity but the baseline “daily full snapshot” model does not use it.
- etcd size is very environment-dependent; for managed Kubernetes we may not back it up at all (or customer handles cluster-level DR separately).


Model 1 (Baseline): Daily FULL snapshot artifact
This is the simplest mental model and matches the current operator expectation (“one artifact per day”).
Formula:
- Raw_total_GB = DB_GB + etcd_GB + k8s_GB
- Artifact_GB = Raw_total_GB * Compression(0.60) * Overhead(1.03)
- Monthly_storage_GB = Artifact_GB * Retention_days
- Monthly_storage_cost = Monthly_storage_GB * $/GB-month

Table 2 — Artifact size per backup (daily full snapshot)
| Deployment size | Raw_total_GB | Artifact_GB (0.60 * 1.03) |
|---|---:|---:|
| S | 25.2 | 15.6 |
| M | 100.3 | 62.0 |
| L | 350.5 | 216.6 |

(Artifact_GB calc: Raw_total_GB * 0.618)

Table 3 — Monthly storage required by retention policy (daily full snapshot)
| Deployment size | 7d retention (GB) | 30d retention (GB) | 90d retention (GB) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S | 109 | 468 | 1,404 |
| M | 434 | 1,860 | 5,580 |
| L | 1,516 | 6,498 | 19,494 |

Table 4 — Estimated monthly storage cost @ $0.023/GB-month (S3 Standard)
| Deployment size | 7d retention ($/mo) | 30d retention ($/mo) | 90d retention ($/mo) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S | 2.50 | 10.76 | 32.29 |
| M | 9.98 | 42.78 | 128.34 |
| L | 34.87 | 149.45 | 448.36 |

Observations:
- For control-plane state, storage cost is usually not the limiting factor; operational correctness + restore validation tends to dominate.
- 90d retention can still be < $500/mo in S3 Standard even at “Large” reference sizes.


Egress model (restore + DR flows)
We model egress as the cost to pull artifacts out of object storage when restoring.
Notes:
- In-region restore (EKS -> S3 same region) often has reduced/no egress; cross-region restore may incur transfer.
- Many customers will replicate backups to a DR region/account; treat that as “daily transfer” volume.

Assumptions for this section:
- Restore drill cadence: 1 restore/week = 4 restores/month
- DR replication cadence: replicate each daily artifact to DR location (30 per month)

Table 5 — Monthly restore drill transfer volume (4 restores/month)
| Deployment size | Artifact_GB | Monthly_GB (4x) |
|---|---:|---:|
| S | 15.6 | 62 |
| M | 62.0 | 248 |
| L | 216.6 | 866 |

Table 6 — Monthly restore drill egress cost @ $0.09/GB (worst-case)
| Deployment size | Monthly_GB | Cost ($/mo) |
|---|---:|---:|
| S | 62 | 5.58 |
| M | 248 | 22.32 |
| L | 866 | 77.94 |

Table 7 — Cross-region replication / DR copy (30 artifacts/month)
| Deployment size | Artifact_GB | Monthly_GB (30x) | Cost @ $0.02/GB (best-ish) | Cost @ $0.09/GB (worst-ish) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S | 15.6 | 468 | 9.36 | 42.12 |
| M | 62.0 | 1,860 | 37.20 | 167.40 |
| L | 216.6 | 6,498 | 129.96 | 584.82 |

Notes:
- The DR copy can cost more than storage depending on network pricing and whether transfer is metered.
- For customers sensitive to transfer cost, recommend same-region restore for “single-region DR” + separate region-copy only for critical tiers.


Sensitivity analysis: alternative backup strategy (Weekly full + daily incremental)
This is a “what if” used for customers who want 90–180d retention without large footprint.
It also reflects how some DB teams think about WAL archiving.

Assumptions for Model 2:
- 1 full snapshot/week (4 full snapshots/month)
- Daily incremental = DB_change + etcd_change + k8s_change
  - etcd_change assumed 5%/day of etcd size (very rough)
  - k8s_change assumed negligible
- Daily incremental is compressed/encrypted with same multipliers

Inputs used:
- DB_daily_change_GB = DB_GB * Daily_change_rate
- etcd_daily_change_GB = etcd_GB * 5%

Table 8 — Incremental artifact size estimate (per day)
| Deployment size | DB_daily_change_GB | etcd_daily_change_GB | Raw_daily_change_GB | Incremental_Artifact_GB (x0.618) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| S | 0.40 | 0.25 | 0.65 | 0.40 |
| M | 1.60 | 1.00 | 2.60 | 1.61 |
| L | 4.50 | 2.50 | 7.00 | 4.33 |

Monthly storage for Model 2 (approx):
- Monthly_GB = (Full_Artifact_GB * Fulls_per_month) + (Incremental_Artifact_GB * Incrementals_per_month)
- Fulls_per_month ~ 4
- Incrementals_per_month ~ 26 (exclude full days)

Table 9 — Model 2 monthly “produced” storage (not retention; just 1 month’s worth)
| Deployment size | Full_Artifact_GB | Incremental_Artifact_GB | Monthly_GB (4*full + 26*incr) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S | 15.6 | 0.40 | 72.8 |
| M | 62.0 | 1.61 | 289.9 |
| L | 216.6 | 4.33 | 979.4 |

Compare to Model 1 monthly produced storage (30*daily full):
| Deployment size | Model 1 monthly GB (30*full) | Model 2 monthly GB | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| S | 468 | 73 | ~84% |
| M | 1,860 | 290 | ~84% |
| L | 6,498 | 979 | ~85% |

Takeaway:
- Weekly-full + daily-incremental can reduce footprint ~5–7x.
- Tradeoff: more complex restore chain (need full + incrementals/WAL to desired point), and higher operator error risk.
- For the current “supported, repeatable” goal, keep Model 1 as default and treat Model 2 as an advanced/opt-in strategy.


Retention sensitivity summary (quick guidance)
- 7d retention:
  - Good default for staging + non-critical tiers.
  - Most useful if restore drills run weekly.
- 30d retention:
  - Good default for enterprise production unless audit/compliance requires longer.
- 90d retention:
  - Usually still affordable on storage; consider lifecycle policy to transition older backups to cheaper tier.
  - Strongly recommend periodic restore validation to avoid “we have backups but they’re unusable.”


Customer-specific knobs to capture (Solutions / SRE intake)
- Backup frequency (daily vs every 6h)
- Retention requirements (7/30/90/180)
- Storage backend (S3+KMS, NFS, GCS)
- Is cross-region DR required? (yes/no; same-account vs cross-account)
- Restore drill requirements (weekly vs monthly; in-prod vs staging)
- Bandwidth constraints (air-gapped export, limited egress)


Worked examples (for SEs)
Example A — Medium (M), 30d retention, daily full:
- Artifact ~ 62 GB/day
- Storage ~ 1,860 GB
- S3 Standard storage cost ~ $42.78/mo
- Restore drill egress (worst-case internet pricing) ~ 248 GB/mo -> $22.32/mo
- Total (storage + drill egress) worst-case ~ $65/mo

Example B — Large (L), 90d retention, daily full + cross-region replication:
- Storage ~ 19,494 GB -> ~$448/mo
- DR copy ~ 6,498 GB/mo transfer
  - If $0.02/GB -> ~$130/mo
  - If $0.09/GB -> ~$585/mo
- Total range (storage + DR transfer) ~ $578–$1,033/mo


Notes / caveats
- If backup artifacts include full audit log exports, numbers can grow significantly (depends on events/day). Treat audit logs as separate cost model.
- If DB includes per-token traces or high-cardinality telemetry, DB growth can dwarf these assumptions (but those should not live in control-plane config DB).
- Compression ratios can vary; if artifacts are already compressed (e.g., protobuf blobs), do not assume 0.60.
- For on-prem NFS, the cost is typically hardware + ops; the sheet is still useful for sizing (GB/TB) even if $ is not meaningful.

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm whether etcd snapshots are in-scope for all Private deployment modes (managed k8s vs self-managed k8s).
- Decide if we should publish a recommended S3 lifecycle policy (e.g., transition >30d to IA/Glacier) as an “enterprise default”.
- Add a second set of tables for “every 6 hours” backup cadence for customers with RPO < 24h.
